Reviewed state · 16 November 2026

What the evidence supports now

The endpoint response ranking change repeats, but the middle point remains mixed. The manuscript now separates that result from service latency, payload effects and memory savings.

0 MiB: Caffeine lower

Response p99.9: 23.8–33.2 µs versus Chronicle’s 281.9–325.1 µs.

Three clean primary pairs.

104 MiB: mixed

Paired Chronicle/Caffeine ratios: 0.427, 0.447, 8.500.

One clean primary pair; clean additional seeds disagree. No further bisection.

208 MiB: Chronicle lower

Response p99.9: 239.2–334.3 µs versus Caffeine’s 921.1–1,188.9 µs.

Three clean primary pairs.

Fresh 4 KiB ordinary get · 512 MiB G1 · 50,000 intended arrivals/s · 30-second offered windows. Ranges span individual forks, not confidence intervals. An observed 0–208 MiB reversal does not locate a precise or universal threshold.

Keep the research questions separate.
  • Ordinary service p99/p99.9: no qualified 4 KiB forward crossover was established in the tested conditions.
  • Response p99.99/p99.999: Chronicle’s advantage already exists at baseline; it is not a pressure-emergent crossover.
  • Payload/RQ2: the focused payload sweeps use different pressure ranges. Movement of a common scheduled-response threshold was not estimated.
  • Memory: lower retained Java heap coexists with higher sampled Chronicle RSS. Equal heap limits are not equal total-memory budgets.
  • Reuse is a separate borrowed-buffer contract. Its sensitivity batches lack a contemporaneous ordinary-Chronicle arm.
  • The primary periodic trace touches 23,169 of 32,768 residents and updates 1,939 distinct keys. Uniform generation is not an unbounded random stream.
  • This compares complete library configurations; the ranking cannot be attributed solely to heap placement.
  • All nine one-second controls lack native CPU coverage; one also has a compiler warning. Their accounting checks do not establish workload host qualification.

Manuscript and review

Working draft, not an author-approved or submitted preprint. The review is agent-assisted, not independent human peer review. The original unconditional Task 12 protocol remains NO_GO.

What the technical review checked

All 162 focused/follow-up observations and 18 primary distributions match their retained audited source inputs. The corrected verifier rejects missing histograms and empty comparisons, checks offered-rate pairing, and remains active under optimized Python.

72 quantile checks · 54 histogram threshold calculations · 270 channel/rate consistency checks · 24 targeted regression tests in the current review; 28 exactly matching offline regenerated outputs were verified in the prior review.

The 16 November host-only pass decoded all 621 focused/follow-up workload and control histograms, reconciled 486 published curves, 4,632 raw-file hashes, 207 GC summaries and all 30 fresh RSS summaries. The original auditor also reproduced its raw-window, GC, bootstrap and 19,782-member archive checks. These remain reproducibility checks, not proof of observer neutrality or event-level causal attribution. Frozen paper data SHA-256: a733eee906a863be68e7fd09ef9e6d3b51cf148ae69f5401c4a0706912ea50b7.

Before a formal release

Independent domain feedback, final typesetting/author revision, clean Java harness reproduction, selected raw-evidence backup/release, and authorship/licensing/disclosure decisions remain open. No additional benchmark is planned for this scoped draft.
